text:
Priya (PM): Quick thread to capture today's post-launch backlog triage + prioritization negotiation. We have three follow-ons from launch feedback: 1) customer request for per-route cached embeddings, 2) a high-frequency low-severity UI annoyance in Console exports, 3) a wishlist ask from Sales for a "preview" routing feature to route high-value customers to a tuned model. Need to decide hotfix vs next sprint vs roadmap.
Noah (Sales): customers A and B asked for per-route embedding cache to speed up repeat searches across their tenants. They see +30% latency on certain routes. This is high-dollar asks.
Gina (CS): confirmation: two enterprise customers hit this, one threat of churn mentioned. They want something within 2 weeks ideally.
Sam (Eng): per-route cache is non-trivial: we need sharding changes + eviction semantics. Rough estimate: 2 engineer-weeks + canary. Could be expedited but will bump other items.
Miko (Design): Console export annoyance: the export button stays enabled and users click multiple times causing confusion. Small UX tweak: disable button after click + add progress state. Quick fix.
Priya (PM): initial proposal: per-route cache -> urgent/hotfix lane (given churn risk) but with a minimal MVP that addresses the immediate customer pain (route-scoped LRU on top of existing prefix cache). Console export -> P2 quick UX patch this sprint. Preview routing feature -> roadmap/backlog (needs policy + billing discussion). Thoughts?
Noah (Sales): routing preview is valuable for enterprise upsell but not urgent. MVP cache would buy time and reduce churn. Can Sales help scope acceptance criteria with customers? We can broker testing.
Gina (CS): we can provide two customers' sample workloads and SLA test cases. Acceptance: median route latency down by 25% and no increase in cache-eviction anomalies for 7 days.
Sam (Eng): technical plan for MVP cache: add per-route cache namespace + LRU with TTL; implement metrics for hit-rate and eviction; limit per-route memory to avoid noisy neighbor. I'll need one backend engineer + one infra on-call to help with canary windows. ETA for MVP: 7 business days with nightly canary.
Priya (PM): acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Per-route cache MVP: 25% median latency improvement for provided customer workloads OR a documented routing workaround + credit if not met in 2 weeks. Canary must show no >1% error delta.
- Console export UX: disable export button on click + spinner + telemetry showing single-click rate >95% within 48h of deploy.
- Preview routing: product spec and billing model by end of next planning cycle (not in next two weeks).
Miko (Design): I'll ship export UX patch as a ~2-hour PR and pair with QA.
Sam (Eng): owners: cache = Sam + Priya; export = Miko + Sam (small infra tweak for rate-limiter); preview routing = Priya + Noah (discovery).
Noah (Sales): we'll run a customer pilot for the cache MVP and commit to testing within 48h of canary. Also will surface pricing sensitivity for preview routing.
release-bot: scheduling canary window for per-route-cache-mvp on dedicated-pool-2 at 03:00 UTC. Notifying owners: Sam, Priya, infra-oncall.
Priya (PM): timeline: per-route cache MVP in hotfix lane; target delivery in 7 business days with canary in 48h of initial build; console export quickpatch in 24-48h; preview routing to product backlog with spec due next planning cycle.
Sam (Eng): small implementation note: will add a debug endpoint to inspect per-route cache stats (`/admin/cache?route=...`) and include a lightweight smoke test command in PR: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings?route=acct-123 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"..."}'
```
Gina (CS): we'll prepare customer workloads and a test harness to validate hit rate and latency. I'll post access details privately.
Miko (Design): will open the export UI PR today and include screenshots for release notes.
Priya (PM): decision log: move per-route cache to hotfix lane (MVP only), console export to quickpatch, preview routing to backlog/spec. I'll update the roadmap board and notify stakeholders.
Noah (Sales): thanks team. If we can get the MVP in 7 days, we can keep the accounts. Happy to help test. :thumbsup:
Priya (PM): thanks all  follow-up sync in 3 days or earlier if canary flags errors.
